\section*{Introduction}

Large-scale image generation has benefited from advances in data scale, quality, rebalancing, and recaptioning, yet conventional pipelines typically optimize task-specific datasets in isolation. A central challenge is not only how to curate each task-specific corpus, but also how to organize heterogeneous supervision according to the dependencies among generative capabilities.

To address this, we introduce a \textbf{capability-driven data infrastructure}: a data curation and training framework that explicitly structures data and supervision around distinct generative capabilities. Here, a \emph{generative capability} refers to a specific function such as text-to-image synthesis, image editing, or image-knowledge association. For example, text-to-image synthesis is the ability to generate an image from a textual description, while image editing involves modifying an image according to a textual instruction, and image-knowledge association links images to structured knowledge entities (e.g., objects or attributes).

\section*{Method}

\subsection*{Capability-Driven Data Infrastructure and Curriculum}

Our infrastructure is guided by a \textbf{capability-aligned curriculum scheduling}, which means that data and training are organized in stages that reflect the prerequisite relationships among these capabilities. For instance, text-to-image grounding is treated as foundational, with editing and knowledge association building upon it. As a concrete example, before constructing editing data (e.g., "change the color of the car from red to blue"), we ensure that the underlying images are reliably paired with accurate captions describing their content.

\subsection*{Data Engines}

The infrastructure comprises three specialized yet interoperable data engines, each responsible for constructing supervision for a specific capability:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Text-Image Grounding Engine}: Pairs images with descriptive captions to support text-to-image generation. For example, an image of a dog playing in a park is paired with the caption "A brown dog runs through green grass in a sunny park."
    \item \textbf{Inter-Image Transformation Engine}: Creates editing pairs by associating source images with their edited counterparts and corresponding transformation instructions. For example, given an original image and an edited version where the sky is changed from cloudy to clear, the engine generates the instruction "make the sky clear" and links the two images.
    \item \textbf{Image-Knowledge Association Engine}: Links images to structured knowledge entities, such as object labels ("dog," "tree") or attributes ("brown," "sunny"), enabling knowledge-grounded generation and retrieval.
\end{enumerate}

These engines share data representations (e.g., unified metadata formats) and enable cross-task supervision by allowing, for example, captions generated for text-to-image pairs to inform editing instructions or knowledge associations. A schematic overview is provided in Figure 1 (not shown here), illustrating the flow of data and supervision among the engines.

\subsection*{Caption Experts}

To ensure consistency and quality across tasks, we employ \textbf{caption experts}: automated captioning models trained to generate high-quality, task-aligned descriptions. For example, a caption expert might generate "A red sports car parked on a city street" for an image, and then produce a transformation instruction like "change the car color to blue" for an editing task. These models harmonize supervision between text-to-image (T2I) and editing tasks, ensuring that captions and transformation instructions are consistent and appropriately granular for each task.

\section*{Data Curation Process}

The data curation process follows a multi-stage curriculum:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Stage 1: Text-to-Image (T2I) Grounding.} Assemble high-quality T2I pairs with broad visual and conceptual coverage. Images are paired with captions generated or verified by caption experts.
    \item \textbf{Stage 2: Editing and Transformation.} Introduce more complex editing tasks by generating editing pairs and transformation instructions for images with reliable T2I grounding.
    \item \textbf{Stage 3: Knowledge Association.} Link images to structured knowledge entities, expanding the dataset's semantic richness.
\end{itemize}

At each stage, data quality, visual-concept diversity, and image resolution are progressively increased. Progression through stages is determined by capability dependencies (e.g., editing data is only constructed for images with reliable T2I grounding) and by quality metrics such as caption accuracy and image fidelity.

\subsection*{Capability-Aware Evaluation}

\textbf{Capability-aware evaluation} is a feedback mechanism that informs the curriculum by identifying gaps in coverage and triggering targeted data retrieval, expert construction, or resampling. Evaluation criteria include:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Coverage Metrics:} Assess the diversity of visual concepts, editing operations, and knowledge entities.
    \item \textbf{Quality Metrics:} Use automated scoring (e.g., CLIP similarity for caption-image alignment, image fidelity scores) and human review to assess data quality.
    \item \textbf{Error Analysis:} Identify failure cases (e.g., inaccurate captions, low-fidelity edits) and prioritize them for data augmentation or expert retraining.
\end{itemize}

Feedback from these evaluations is used to adjust data sampling, retrain caption experts, or expand underrepresented categories.
